title: Oakridge Data - Retainer renewal and multi-region upgrade check-in
next_steps: Send updated pricing worksheet with 12-month retainer tier and burst buckets
Share SOC 2 + ISO27001 attestation and KMS/HSM integration notes
Schedule technical benchmark for p99 latency with their RLHF models (Luis + Tom) - target week of Sep 13
action_items: Maya - send pricing worksheet and go/no-go timeline; due 2026-09-03
Luis - run preliminary perf checklist and confirm required GPU profile for 1.2x throughput; due 2026-09-10
Nina - share internal compliance questions list for SOC2+data residency; due 2026-09-07
summary: Customer is evaluating renewing their retainer at a higher tier to add EU region activation and an APAC burst pool. Main concerns are latency for inference in EU (p99 targets), data residency / audit logs, and fallback behavior to hosted variants. Redwood AE + SE proposed a 12-month retainer with reserved burst capacity, offered next-step benchmarks and security docs.
topics: EU region activation and data residency
questions: What are p99 SLA numbers if we add EU region?
How does private VPC deployment affect rollout timing?
Do we have key rotation practices for customer-managed KMS?
transcript:
00:00:03 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep to 40 minutes, agenda is renewal, region activation, and a quick ops check. Sara you good with that?
00:00:12 Sara Patel: Yep fine, thanks. We have folks from security and platform on to make sure timing is realistic.
00:00:20 Tom Ellis: Morning all, quick note, we've got a big Q4 release so timeline's tight. We want EU active by Oct 15 ideally.
00:00:30 Maya Chen: OK noted. Luis, do you want to start with the perf picture?
00:00:36 Luis Rivera: Sure. Quick recap: current retainer is 500k token units, single US region. From telemetry we see steady-state 25ms token latency for our baseline model but p99 spikes up to 420ms under certain batching. If Oakridge wants EU p99 target at 350ms we'd recommend either reserved EU capacity or a mixed routing policy with prefix cache warmed.
00:01:02 Tom Ellis: 420ms p99, is that with cross-region KV cache cold? Because our traffic is mostly EU users, so routing us-west to EU will kill us.
00:01:13 Luis Rivera: Right, that's exactly the pattern. With a dedicated EU pool we can get p99 into the 280-330ms range depending on model and sequence length distribution. There's also a quantized variant which reduces GPU memory footprint and improves throughput but sometimes increases latency jitter slightly.
00:01:32 Sara Patel: Hmm, we use an internal RLHF model variant, longer context windows — like 2k tokens average. Does Redwood's quant path support that without quality regressions?
00:01:41 Luis Rivera: Good question. We do per-model quant profiles — we'd run a quant eval on your sample prompts. Usually for longer contexts we caution about 4-bit aggressive quantization; we suggest 8-bit plus mixed-float kernel for your workload. That preserves output quality while giving cost benefits.
00:01:56 Ajay Singh: Cost is a big part. If we reserve EU capacity what does pricing look like compared to bursting?
00:02:03 Maya Chen: We have a 12-month retainer tier we can upsell you to — it includes reserved EU nodes and a burst bucket for APAC traffic. The math depends on commit level; I'll send a worksheet after this call. Net-net: reserved capacity lowers unit cost 18-30% vs pure on-demand/burst.
00:02:24 Tom Ellis: And the burst bucket for APAC — is that reachable within existing network peering or do we need additional infra?
00:02:30 Luis Rivera: For APAC burst we usually provision regional nodes in the edge cluster; no customer infra change except for CIDR and VPC peering in the Private deployment option. For Hosted, it's fully managed, just a routing policy change.
00:02:43 Nina Gomez: Security question — we need audit logs and customer-managed KMS. How does the key rotation work and can we see detailed audit trails for token-level access?
00:02:53 Maya Chen: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS in Private and in Dedicated with an HSM-backed option on certain plans. Audit logs are available via the Console with token-level traces — retention tiers vary by add-on.
00:03:06 Nina Gomez: Is SOC 2 available? We need the attestation for procurement.
00:03:10 Maya Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 are available; I'll attach the latest attestations and the compliance pack.
00:03:18 Sara Patel: Great. Back to timelines — Oct 15 for EU is our target. What are realistic lead times?
00:03:24 Luis Rivera: For Hosted with reserved EU capacity, assuming commit signed, we can stage within 2-3 weeks for a standard model. If you want a Private VPC activation, plan 6-8 weeks for networking, KMS, and customer-side approvals.
00:03:39 Tom Ellis: That's tight. Procurement will need a signed SOW before staging. Can we get a draft SOW and a sample runbook?
00:03:46 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include SOW templates and a runbook. Also we'll propose a canary activation: start with replicated read traffic then full routing.
00:03:55 Ajay Singh: About fallback behavior — if EU pool hits capacity do you have automatic fallback to hosted or to smaller model variants? We can't have 503s.
00:04:03 Luis Rivera: We have smart routing policies: fallback to compatible model variants or to other regions with graceful degradation. We also have automatic rate-limited bursting and queuing strategies. We'll show you an example policy config.
00:04:16 Sara Patel: Regarding model variants — earlier we tested a smaller decoder and saw hallucinations increase; we need regression gates. Can Redwood tie regressions to prompt/eval sets?
00:04:27 Luis Rivera: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run prompt set-based quality monitors and trigger alerts on regression thresholds. We can set an approval gate before routing to the quantized variant.
00:04:37 Tom Ellis: Ok good. Next: billing and invoicing cadence — we prefer monthly invoice with usage reconciliation. Does the retainer support that?
00:04:45 Maya Chen: Yes, we can structure the retainer as monthly invoices against the committed units with overage billed monthly. We can also do quarterly true-ups for account governance.
00:04:55 Nina Gomez: A nit — data residency. If EU region is active, do logs or KVS ever leave region? We need strict residency for certain PII flows.
00:05:03 Luis Rivera: For Dedicated and Private, we can guarantee storage and logs remain in the region; for Hosted we do regional controls but need to check for aggregated telemetry transfers — I'll confirm specifics.
00:05:14 Sara Patel: Can we get a diagram of the network path and where logs live?
00:05:18 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include an architecture diagram in the docs we share.
00:05:23 Ajay Singh: On the technical benchmark — we want p50, p95, p99 for our RLHF model and cost per 1k tokens with reserved capacity vs burst. Luis will drive that?
00:05:32 Luis Rivera: Yep I'll run a focused perf run with your model snapshot. I'll need tokenization sample and a small dataset. Expect a 1-week turnaround once we have samples and access.
00:05:42 Tom Ellis: Access — do you need an S3 bucket with sample inputs or can we paste a subset?
00:05:47 Luis Rivera: S3 is preferred for scale, but a zipped sample via secure link works. We'll also need approximate concurrency profile.
00:05:56 Maya Chen: Action recap: I'll send pricing + SOW + compliance pack today. Luis will start perf checklist when they send samples. Nina will send compliance Qs. We'll plan a follow-up tech benchmark next week.
00:06:07 Sara Patel: Sounds good. Any objections from procurement?
00:06:10 Tom Ellis: Procurement will push on termination language and data deletion guarantees. We'll add those to Nina's list.
00:06:16 Maya Chen: Noted. Anything else?
00:06:19 Speaker 5: quick question on rate limiting — can token bucket rules be per-route?
00:06:23 Luis Rivera: Yes per-route quotas and per-token classes, and token-level cost tagging.
00:06:29 Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark.
00:06:34 Sara Patel: Thanks, bye.
00:06:36 Tom Ellis: Bye.
00:06:40 Maya Chen: Closing now.

Notes: transcript includes natural pauses and occasional mis-attributions. Some model and product names slightly transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" as "K-V cache" in places).
